<summary><h2> What Can I Do with Hyperswitch?</h2></summary>

Hyperswitch offers a modular, open-source payments infrastructure designed for flexibility and control. Apart from our Payment Suite offering, this solution allows businesses to pick and integrate only the modules they need on top of their existing payment stack — without unnecessary complexity or vendor lock-in.

Each module is independent and purpose-built to optimize different aspects of payment processing.

<h3> Learn More About The Payment Modules </h3>
<details>

- **Cost Observability**  
  Advanced observability tools to audit, monitor, and optimize your payment costs. Detect hidden fees, downgrades, and penalties with self-serve dashboards and actionable insights.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/ai-powered-cost-observability)_

- **Revenue Recovery**  
  Combat passive churn with intelligent retry strategies tuned by card bin, region, method, and more. Offers fine-grained control over retry algorithms, penalty budgets, and recovery transparency.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/revenue-recovery)_

- **Vault**  
  A PCI-compliant vault service to store cards, tokens, wallets, and bank credentials. Provides a unified, secure, and reusable store of customer-linked payment methods.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/vault)_

- **Intelligent Routing**  
  Route each transaction to the PSP with the highest predicted auth rate. Reduce retries, avoid downtime, and minimize latency while maximizing first attempt success.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/intelligent-routing)_

- **Reconciliation**  
  Automate 2-way and 3-way reconciliation with backdated support, staggered scheduling, and customizable outputs. Reduces manual ops effort and increases audit confidence.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/reconciliation)_

- **Alternate Payment Methods**  
  Drop-in widgets for PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay, Pay by Bank, and BNPL providers like Klarna. Maximizes conversions with seamless one-click checkout.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/enable-alternate-payment-method-widgets)_

</details>

## Quickstart 

<h3> Local Setup via Docker </h3>

```bash
# One-click local setup

git clone --depth 1 --branch latest https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch

cd hyperswitch

scripts/setup.sh
```
<details>
  <summary><strong>This script: </strong></summary>

  - Detects Docker/Podman  
  - Offers multiple deployment profiles:
    - **Standard**: App server + Control Center  
    - **Full**: Includes monitoring + schedulers  
    - **Minimal**: Standalone App server  
  - Provides access links when done

  If you need further help, check out our [video tutorial](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/overview/unified-local-setup-using-docker).  

  👉 After setup, [configure a connector](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/account-setup/using-hyperswitch-control-center#add-a-payment-processor) and [test a payment](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/account-setup/test-a-payment).
</details>


<h3>Hosted Sandbox (No Setup Required)</h3>

Hyperswitch offers a fully hosted sandbox environment that requires no setup. You can explore the Control Center, configure payment connectors, and test payments directly from the UI.

   <a href="https://app.hyperswitch.io">
     <img src="https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch/blob/main/docs/imgs/try-the-sandbox.png?raw=true" height="35">
   </a>


<details>
  <summary><strong> What you can do in the Hosted Sandbox</strong></summary>

  - Access the full Control Center  
  - Configure payment connectors  
  - View logs, routing rules, and retry strategies  
  - Try payments directly from the UI  
</details>

You can deploy to AWS, GCP, or Azure using Helm or CDK scripts. Fastest path:

Click to deploy via AWS:

## Why Hyperswitch?

Hyperswitch is a commercial open-source payments stack purpose-built for scale, flexibility, and developer experience. Designed with a modular architecture, Hyperswitch lets you pick only the components you need—whether it’s routing, retries, vaulting, or observability—without vendor lock-in or bloated integrations.

Built in Rust for performance and reliability, Hyperswitch supports global payment methods (cards, wallets, BNPL, UPI, Pay by Bank), exposes smart routing and retry logic, and provides a visual workflow builder in the Control Center. Whether you're integrating a full payment suite or augmenting an existing stack with a single module, Hyperswitch meets you where you are.

<strong>“Linux for Payments”</strong> — Hyperswitch is a well-architected reference for teams who want to own their payments stack.

We believe in:

- <strong> Embracing Payment Diversity:</strong> Innovation comes from enabling choice—across payment methods, processors, and flows.

- <strong> Open Source by Default:</strong> Transparency drives trust and builds better, reusable software.

- <strong> Community-Driven Development:</strong> Our roadmap is shaped by real-world use cases and contributors. 

- <strong> Systems-Level Engineering:</strong> We hold ourselves to a high bar for reliability, security, and performance.

- <strong> Maximizing Value Creation:</strong> For developers, customers, and partners alike.

- <strong> Community-Driven, Enterprise-Tested:</strong> Hyperswitch is built in the open with real-world feedback from developers and contributors, and maintained by Juspay, the team powering payment infrastructure for 400+ leading enterprises worldwide.

We welcome contributors from around the world to help build Hyperswitch. Whether you're fixing bugs, improving documentation, or adding new features, your help is appreciated.

Please read our [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch/blob/main/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) to get started.

565: pub fn build_payload(
566:     method: String,
567:     path: &str,
568:     headers: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
569:     body: Option<&str>,
570: ) -> String {
571:     let mut payload = format!("{} {}\n", method.to_uppercase(), normalize_path(path));
572: 
573:     for (k, v) in headers {
574:         payload.push_str(&format!("{}: {}\n", k, v));
575:     }
576: 
577:     if let Some(body_str) = body {
578:         payload.push_str(body_str);
579:     }
580: 
581:     payload
582: }

584: pub fn generate_tl_signature(
585:     method: String,
586:     path: &str,
587:     headers: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
588:     body: Option<&str>,
589:     private_key: String,
590:     kid: &str,
591: ) -> common_utils::errors::CustomResult<String, errors::ConnectorError> {
592:     let payload = build_payload(method, path, headers, body);
593:     let pem = utils::base64_decode(private_key)?;
594: 
595:     let signer = ES512.signer_from_pem(&pem).change_context(
596:         errors::ConnectorError::RequestEncodingFailedWithReason(
597:             "Failed to generate Tl-Signature".to_string(),
598:         ),
599:     )?;
600: 
601:     let tl_headers = headers.keys().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(",");
602: 
603:     let mut header = JwsHeader::new();
604:     header.set_algorithm("ES512");
605:     header.set_key_id(kid);
606:     header
607:         .set_claim("tl_version", Some("2".into()))
608:         .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::RequestEncodingFailedWithReason(
609:             "Failed to generate Tl-Signature".to_string(),
610:         ))?;
611:     header
612:         .set_claim("tl_headers", Some(tl_headers.into()))
613:         .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::RequestEncodingFailedWithReason(
614:             "Failed to generate Tl-Signature".to_string(),
615:         ))?;
616: 
617:     let jws = josekit::jws::serialize_compact(payload.as_bytes(), &header, &signer)
618:         .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::RequestEncodingFailedWithReason(
619:             "Failed to generate Tl-Signature".to_string(),
620:         ))?;
621: 
622:     let parts: Vec<&str> = jws.split('.').collect();
623: 
624:     match (parts.first(), parts.get(2)) {
625:         (Some(first), Some(third)) => Ok(format!("{}..{}", first, third)),
626:         _ => Err(errors::ConnectorError::RequestEncodingFailedWithReason(
627:             "Failed to generate Tl-Signature".to_string(),
628:         )
629:         .into()),
630:     }
631: }

744: fn pad_to(bytes: Vec<u8>, target: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, errors::ConnectorError> {
745:     match bytes.len().cmp(&target) {
746:         std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => Ok(bytes),
747:         std::cmp::Ordering::Less => {
748:             let mut padded = vec![0u8; target - bytes.len()];
749:             padded.extend(bytes);
750:             Ok(padded)
751:         }
752:         std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => Err(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed),
753:     }
754: }
755: 
756: fn headermap_to_hashmap(headers: &HeaderMap) -> HashMap<String, String> {
757:     let mut map = HashMap::new();
758: 
759:     for (key, value) in headers.iter() {
760:         if let Ok(value_str) = value.to_str() {
761:             map.insert(key.to_string(), value_str.to_string());
762:         }
763:     }
764: 
765:     map
766: }
767: 
768: fn verify_signature(
769:     body: &[u8],
770:     jws_header: JwsHeaderWebhooks,
771:     header_b64: &str,
772:     signature_b64: &str,
773:     headers: &HashMap<String, String>,
774:     ec_key: &EcKey<Public>,
775:     webhook_uri: &str,
776: ) -> Result<bool, error_stack::Report<errors::ConnectorError>> {
777:     let tl_headers_str = jws_header.tl_headers.unwrap_or_default();
778:     let mut payload: Vec<u8> = format!("{} {}\n", "POST".to_uppercase(), webhook_uri).into_bytes();
779: 
780:     if !tl_headers_str.is_empty() {
781:         let lower_headers: HashMap<String, &String> =
782:             headers.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.to_lowercase(), v)).collect();
783:         for header_name in tl_headers_str.split(',') {
784:             let name = header_name.trim();
785:             let value = lower_headers
786:                 .get(&name.to_lowercase())
787:                 .ok_or(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
788:             payload.extend_from_slice(format!("{}: {}\n", name, value).as_bytes());
789:         }
790:     }
791:     payload.extend_from_slice(body);
792: 
793:     // signing_input = base64url(header) + "." + base64url(payload)
794:     let signing_input = format!("{}.{}", header_b64, URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(&payload));
795: 
796:     // Convert P1363 signature (r || s, 66 bytes each) to DER
797:     let sig_bytes = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
798:         .decode(signature_b64)
799:         .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
800:     if sig_bytes.len() != 132 {
801:         return Err(report!(
802:             errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed
803:         ));
804:     }
805: 
806:     let r = BigNum::from_slice(
807:         sig_bytes
808:             .get(0..66)
809:             .ok_or(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?,
810:     )
811:     .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
812:     let s = BigNum::from_slice(
813:         sig_bytes
814:             .get(66..)
815:             .ok_or(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?,
816:     )
817:     .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
818:     let der_sig = EcdsaSig::from_private_components(r, s)
819:         .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?
820:         .to_der()
821:         .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
822: 
823:     // SHA-512 digest + ECDSA verify
824:     let digest = hash(MessageDigest::sha512(), signing_input.as_bytes())
825:         .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
826: 
827:     let ecdsa_sig = EcdsaSig::from_der(&der_sig)
828:         .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
829: 
830:     let valid = ecdsa_sig
831:         .verify(&digest, ec_key)
832:         .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
833: 
834:     Ok(valid)
835: }

837: impl
838:     TryFrom<
839:         ResponseRouterData<
840:             VerifyWebhookSource,
841:             Jwks,
842:             VerifyWebhookSourceRequestData,
843:             VerifyWebhookSourceResponseData,
844:         >,
845:     > for VerifyWebhookSourceRouterData
846: {
847:     type Error = error_stack::Report<errors::ConnectorError>;
848:     fn try_from(
849:         item: ResponseRouterData<
850:             VerifyWebhookSource,
851:             Jwks,
852:             VerifyWebhookSourceRequestData,
853:             VerifyWebhookSourceResponseData,
854:         >,
855:     ) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
856:         let body = item.data.request.webhook_body.as_ref();
857:         let headers = headermap_to_hashmap(&item.data.request.webhook_headers);
858: 
859:         let tl_signature_header = item
860:             .data
861:             .request
862:             .webhook_headers
863:             .get("Tl-Signature")
864:             .ok_or(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSignatureNotFound)?;
865:         let tl_signature = tl_signature_header
866:             .to_str()
867:             .map_err(|_| errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSignatureNotFound)?;
868:         let parts: Vec<&str> = tl_signature.splitn(3, '.').collect();
869: 
870:         let header_b64 = parts
871:             .first()
872:             .ok_or(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
873:         let signature_b64 = parts
874:             .get(2)
875:             .ok_or(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
876: 
877:         let header_json = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
878:             .decode(header_b64)
879:             .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
880:         let jws_header: JwsHeaderWebhooks = serde_json::from_slice(&header_json)
881:             .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
882: 
883:         let jwk = item
884:             .response
885:             .keys
886:             .into_iter()
887:             .find(|k| k.kid == jws_header.kid && k.kty == "EC")
888:             .ok_or(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
889: 
890:         let x_raw = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
891:             .decode(
892:                 jwk.x
893:                     .ok_or(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?,
894:             )
895:             .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
896:         let y_raw = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
897:             .decode(
898:                 jwk.y
899:                     .ok_or(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?,
900:             )
901:             .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
902: 
903:         let mut sec1 = vec![0x04u8];
904:         sec1.extend(pad_to(x_raw, 66)?);
905:         sec1.extend(pad_to(y_raw, 66)?);
906: 
907:         let group = EcGroup::from_curve_name(Nid::SECP521R1)
908:             .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
909:         let mut ctx = BigNumContext::new()
910:             .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
911:         let point = EcPoint::from_bytes(&group, &sec1, &mut ctx)
912:             .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
913:         let ec_key = EcKey::from_public_key(&group, &point)
914:             .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
915:         ec_key
916:             .check_key()
917:             .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::WebhookSourceVerificationFailed)?;
918:         let webhook_uri = item.data.request.webhook_uri.to_string();
919: 
920:         let valid = verify_signature(
921:             body,
922:             jws_header.clone(),
923:             header_b64,
924:             signature_b64,
925:             &headers,
926:             &ec_key,
927:             &(PREFIX.to_owned() + &webhook_uri),
928:         )? || verify_signature(
929:             body,
930:             jws_header.clone(),
931:             header_b64,
932:             signature_b64,
933:             &headers,
934:             &ec_key,
935:             &webhook_uri,
936:         )?;
937: 
938:         Ok(Self {
939:             response: Ok(VerifyWebhookSourceResponseData {
940:                 verify_webhook_status: if valid {
941:                     VerifyWebhookStatus::SourceVerified
942:                 } else {
943:                     VerifyWebhookStatus::SourceNotVerified
944:                 },
945:             }),
946:             ..item.data
947:         })
948:     }

380:         }
381:         serde_json::Value::Array(arr) => arr.iter().map(serialize_data).collect(),
382:         serde_json::Value::String(s) => s.clone(),
383:         serde_json::Value::Number(n) => n.to_string(),
384:         serde_json::Value::Bool(b) => b.to_string(),
385:         serde_json::Value::Null => String::new(),
386:     }
387: }

389: pub fn generate_trustly_signature<T: Serialize>(
390:     method: &str,
391:     uuid: &str,
392:     data: &T,
393:     private_key: &str,
394: ) -> Result<String, ConnectorError> {
395:     let algorithm = Algorithm::SHA256;
396:     let pem = utils::base64_decode(private_key.to_string())
397:         .map_err(|_| ConnectorError::RequestEncodingFailed)?;
398:     let rsa = Rsa::private_key_from_pem(&pem).map_err(|_| ConnectorError::RequestEncodingFailed)?;
399:     let private_key = PKey::from_rsa(rsa).map_err(|_| ConnectorError::RequestEncodingFailed)?;
400: 
401:     let plaintext = format!("{}{}{}", method, uuid, trustly_serialize(data));
402: 
403:     let mut signer = Signer::new(algorithm.message_digest(), &private_key)
404:         .map_err(|_| ConnectorError::RequestEncodingFailed)?;
405:     signer
406:         .update(plaintext.as_bytes())
407:         .map_err(|_| ConnectorError::RequestEncodingFailed)?;
408:     let signature = signer
409:         .sign_to_vec()
410:         .map_err(|_| ConnectorError::RequestEncodingFailed)?;
411: 
412:     Ok(format!(
413:         "{}{}",
414:         algorithm.prefix(),
415:         general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(&signature)
416:     ))
417: }

419: fn serialize_data(value: &serde_json::Value) -> String {
420:     match value {
421:         serde_json::Value::Object(map) => {
422:             // BTreeMap keeps keys sorted (matches PHP's ksort)
423:             let sorted: BTreeMap<_, _> = map.iter().collect();
424:             sorted
425:                 .iter()
426:                 .fold(String::new(), |mut output, (key, value)| {
427:                     output.push_str(key);
428:                     output.push_str(&serialize_data(value));
429:                     output
430:                 })
431:         }
432:         serde_json::Value::Array(arr) => arr.iter().map(serialize_data).collect(),
433:         serde_json::Value::String(s) => s.clone(),
434:         serde_json::Value::Number(n) => n.to_string(),
435:         serde_json::Value::Bool(b) => b.to_string(),
436:         serde_json::Value::Null => String::new(),
437:     }
438: }

part.text:
The changes are complete. Here's a summary of the patch:

**1. Deferred capture support for both connectors:**
- `crates/hyperswitch_connectors/src/connectors/truelayer.rs`: Added `CaptureMethod::Manual` to `supported_capture_methods`
- `crates/hyperswitch_connectors/src/connectors/trustly.rs`: Added `CaptureMethod::Manual` to `supported_capture_methods`

**2. Removed location requirement for Trustly:**
- `crates/payment_methods/src/configs/payment_connector_required_fields.rs`: Added `Connector::Trustly` to `PaymentMethodType::Trustly` with only `billing_name()` (first name + last name), explicitly excluding any `BillingAddressCountries` or address-based location constraints

**3. Added customer data validation for both connectors:**
- `crates/payment_methods/src/configs/payment_connector_required_fields.rs`: Added `Connector::Truelayer` to `PaymentMethodType::OpenBanking` with `billing_name()` required fields
- `crates/payment_methods/src/configs/payment_connector_required_fields.rs`: Added `Connector::Trustly` to `PaymentMethodType::Trustly` with `billing_name()` required fields

The patch ensures both connectors can now handle deferred (manual) capture workflows and have proper validation configured to collect essential customer billing name information during payment processing, while Trustly specifically no longer mandates location/address details upfront.
